opening.headline: Learn why permissions are unstable when you want to let AI handle mail, documents, and calendars directly, and how to distinguish between app connection and agent permissions.
body: I think it would be convenient to find and summarize the emails I received, organize them in a document, and even set a schedule. However, I hesitate to entrust it to AI because it is difficult to know what it can see in my account and whether it only reads or sends emails.

In this class, we will look at how ChatGPT's app connection process is performed, how reading and execution are divided after connection, and what permission options control the human confirmation steps before execution. Lastly, we explain the points that need to be confirmed in the case of entrusting 'sending reservation emails' to an agent.
objectives: Can explain the role of app connectivity and agent functions
You can distinguish between read permission, execution permission, and whether approval is required.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

screens.title: I want to leave my emails, documents, and calendars to you, but
screens.lead: We take a look at the anxiety that often arises when you want to entrust your work to AI. When you select each item, an explanation will unfold.

items.prompt: What do you want to be entrusted with?
items.answer: This is a flow that finds and summarizes received emails, organizes the results in a document, and even sets a schedule if necessary. I want to be able to do things I used to do by going back and forth between multiple apps with a single conversation.

The downside is that it's difficult to know what the AI can see in your account. It's difficult to entrust it to someone if it's not clear how to check whether they're only seeing what they need to see or whether they're seeing other folders or emails as well.

items.prompt: Are reading and execution the same thing?
items.answer: It's different. Finding and reading mail is reading, and sending mail or changing schedules is execution, which changes the state of the other service. Reading can be redone if you make a mistake, but execution can be difficult to reverse.

items.prompt: What is the crux of the problem?
items.answer: The point is that the size of authority and responsibility for execution are mixed together. If you look at these two separately, you can decide where to stop and check.

screens.outro: First, let's recall the login permissions I've already given you.

screens.title: Recall: the login permissions I gave you
screens.lead: Read the questions and think for yourself first. There is no need to submit an answer, and when you select an item, the instructor's thoughts unfold.

items.prompt: Is there an AI service that gives login permission to external apps?
items.answer: You may have experience connecting with AI services by logging in with your Google account or Slack. At that time, it may seem like it's usually just a single 'Connect' button, but in reality, you've given permission to access your account.

items.prompt: Do you remember what permission list you saw back then?
items.answer: Not many people read the permission list carefully and approve it. The goal in this lesson is to remember that the approval screen lists services and permissions, and to get into the habit of reading what is being requested before approving it.

items.prompt: Who is responsible if an AI sends something in my name?
items.answer: AI operates within the range I allow. So how much I allow ultimately depends on the settings I set. Connection is a matter of giving authority, and the responsibility for execution returns to the person who gave the authority.

screens.outro: Now, let's take a step-by-step look at how app connection takes place.

screens.title: App Linking: Link accounts and review permissions
screens.lead: The following steps describe the procedure for connecting apps in ChatGPT. Select the next arrow and follow what you need to see at each step.

visual.alt: Flowchart for selecting a plugin in settings, linking an account, and reviewing permissions.
labels: Permission granted = The moment access is granted.

steps.title: Understand what the app does
steps.body: The app brings services you already use, like Google Drive or Slack, into your ChatGPT conversations. Depending on the app, you can find files, summarize documents, or look up messages. Some apps display screens such as maps or cards, or directly perform actions supported by connected services.

steps.title: Choose an app or plugin in Settings
steps.body: Open Plugins in Settings and select the app you want to connect to, or the plugin that contains the app. In very old iOS or Android apps, they may appear as Apps instead of Plugins. If you see Install plugin, select it, which may also start the app connection or setup process.

steps.title: Connect to my account
steps.body: Select Connect or continue through the app's setup process. If the app requires individual authentication, sign in with an account that already has permission to access the information you want to use. Some apps do not require individual logins or use connections set up by administrators.

steps.title: Review requested services and permissions
steps.body: The provider's authentication screen lists the services and permissions being requested. Read this list before approving. Some providers include related services together in the same authentication flow, which should be reviewed for each service you select. In fact, the actions available in ChatGPT also depend on the app's functionality and workspace settings.

steps.title: Pitfalls of account selection
steps.body: Even if you link your personal account, you won't be able to access files, channels, or records that exist only in your work account. Conversely, you need to link accounts with information to get the desired results. Additionally, installing the plugin does not replace account verification or workspace authorization. To use the app, you must have access to the app, the correct linked account, and all necessary provider approvals.

steps.title: Manage after connection
steps.body: To check the connection later, select the app or linked account under Plugins in Settings. Depending on the app, you can connect multiple accounts, and disconnect apps you no longer use. In a managed workspace, your administrator may need to turn on the app or approve the account domain.

screens.outro: Once connected, the next question is when does ChatGPT ask and when does it run immediately?

screens.title: Permission options and agent approval steps
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn about the differences in permission options and authorization in agent features.

tabs.label: Always ask
tabs.body: ChatGPT asks before reading or changing app information. This is the most conservative setting. It is suitable for those who are using the app for the first time or have a lot of business-sensitive information, and instead, the approval screen appears frequently.

tabs.label: Allow read actions
tabs.body: ChatGPT will read without asking, but will ask before making any changes. Reading operations, such as retrieving mail or viewing documents, are frequently necessary and low risk, so it's a balance of allowing changes to be confirmed while increasing convenience. In some menus, this is abbreviated to Allow read.

tabs.label: Allow low-risk actions
tabs.body: Automatically approve low-risk tasks and require confirmation or reject high-risk tasks. This setting only applies if the policy for your account, workspace, app, or connection isn't overwritten. An operation is considered high risk by whether it affects other services, reveals sensitive information, or is difficult to reverse.

tabs.label: Allow all actions
tabs.body: Perform supported actions without additional approval. The document states that this option carries high risks. This option is not available in standard account-wide settings and workspace-wide settings; it may only appear in individual apps or linked accounts.

tabs.label: Limitations of Permission Options
tabs.body: Permission settings only control when ChatGPT asks you when using the app. It does not link accounts, grant provider permissions, change access scope of the source system, or overwrite workspace policies. Actions that affect other services, such as sending mail, posting messages, sending invitations, or editing and deleting files, may be subject to additional review.

tabs.label: Agent-like functions
tabs.body: ChatGPT Work is an agent-like experience that entrusts you with long, multi-step tasks and completed results. The previous ChatGPT agent mode is no longer available and ChatGPT Work has taken over that role. Business and enterprise workspaces allow you to create workspace agents for repetitive tasks. It is used by connecting an app and a tool. By default, the app's writing behavior is set to Always ask, and only authorized users can view the agent according to role-based access control.

screens.outro: Now that we have seen the permission options and the agent's approval structure, let's actually solve one request.

screens.title: Explanatory example: When leaving the ‘sending reservation email’ to an agent
screens.lead: The instructor shows the process of processing a request to 'Send a schedule change email to my business partner tomorrow morning.' Select the next arrow to follow the confirmation points one by one.

steps.title: View requests
steps.body: The request is ‘Send a schedule change email to my business partner tomorrow morning.’ It's just one sentence, but it includes finding customer contact information, checking previous emails, writing the body, setting a sending time, and sending. Before assigning a task, you need to determine whether these actions are reading or executing.

steps.title: Step 1: Divide between reading and doing
steps.body: Finding contacts and reading old emails is reading. If you make a mistake, you can do it again and the status of the other service will not change. On the other hand, sending an email is an action that changes the state of the other service, and is difficult to reverse once it reaches the recipient. This distinction is the standard for all subsequent judgments.

steps.title: Step 2: Verify your linked accounts
steps.body: If you are sending a business email to a business partner, your business account must be connected. If only your personal account is connected, contacts or email records that exist only in your work account will not be visible, and there is a risk that email will be sent from the wrong address. First check which account is connected with what permissions in Settings.

steps.title: Step 3: Set permission options
steps.body: Since reads are frequently required, you can reduce repeated approvals by setting Allow read actions. Changes such as sending are always requested or read-only, so the content is checked and approved each time. For convenience, if you set it to Allow all actions, there is a high risk that it may be sent without confirmation. If it's a managed workspace, workspace policies take precedence.

steps.title: Step 4: Human verification before shipping
steps.body: When the authorization screen appears, read the app, account, and suggested actions. A person personally checks whether the recipient is correct, whether the sending time is as intended, and whether the schedule and expression of the text are accurate. If you are not sure, decline with Deny or Decline and request modification. If you use Allow once, only this action will be approved and you will be asked again in the future.

steps.title: Step 5: Be careful when entrusting it as an agent
steps.body: When assigning recurring tasks to an agent or workspace agent, you must also decide on an authentication method to connect the app. There are two methods: each person running the service authenticates using their own account, and the agent uses a public connection. If possible, use a service account for the public connection and allow only necessary access. Be sure to set the write operation to safe for dangerous flows.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: The conclusion of this case is one line: Connection is permission, execution is responsibility. Reading is conveniently allowed, but hard-to-revert changes, such as sending and editing, are approved after a person checks the content. By following this order, you can delegate tasks to AI without obscuring where ultimate responsibility lies. In the same way, event invitations or file deletion requests can be divided into read and execute. If you see options such as Deny, Allow once, or Always allow on the approval screen, also read whether you want to allow this once or continuously in the future.

screens.outro: Now that I've identified the points that need confirmation, I'll organize the class.

screens.title: Summary: Connection is authority, execution is responsibility.
screens.lead: Let's summarize what we've seen so far. Read on to think about what tasks you should not take on without approval.

paragraphs: App linking is a grant of permission to bring information and actions from an external service into your conversation. When connecting, log in with the correct account with your information and read the requested services and permissions before approving them. Installing the plugin does not replace account verification.

After connection, reading and execution are separated. Reading is simply retrieving information, and executing is changing the state of the other service. Permission options are arranged in decreasing order of approval levels, from Always ask to Allow all actions, and the higher you go, the more convenient but also the more risky.

Agent-like features use apps and tools to carry out long tasks in multiple steps, making setting app permissions and approvals even more important. Changes, such as sending e-mails, are allowed only after confirming the contents.
Please also remember that permission settings do not change account linking or provider permissions, nor can they overwrite workspace policies.

Before using a new app or agent, there are three questions to ask: What account does it connect to? Is it only readable or executable? Do I check it before executing it? If you can answer these three questions, most of your anxiety will turn into a specific setup issue. This changed problem can be resolved in settings.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: When using the app with an agent, the document advises to take special care to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive information.

glossary.def: This is a connection that brings information from an external service into the conversation and performs supported actions.
This is the right to only view information. It does not change the state of the other service.
This is the right to perform actions that change the status of the other service, such as sending messages or modifying files.
This is the stage where a person views the content and approves or rejects it before execution.
This is the ability to use apps and tools to perform multi-step tasks on your own. These include ChatGPT Work and Workspace Agent.

misconceptions.myth: When you install the plugin, access rights are automatically granted.
misconceptions.fact: Installing the plugin does not replace account verification or workspace authorization. Requires separate app access, correct linked account, and necessary provider approvals.

misconceptions.myth: If you connect your personal account, you can also view your work files.
misconceptions.fact: Only the range accessible to the connected account is visible. Even if you link your personal account, you won't be able to access files, channels, or records that exist only in your work account.

misconceptions.myth: It is more convenient and there are no problems if you disable all approval settings.
misconceptions.fact: Allow all actions is risky because it performs supported actions without permission. For tasks that are difficult to reverse, such as sending an email, it is safer to leave a confirmation step.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: The connection is an authorization, so it verifies and approves the correct account and requested permissions.
Reading and execution are distinguished, and execution requires user confirmation.
Permission options are in decreasing order of approval levels, from Always ask to Allow all actions, with the higher the number, the greater the risk.
Changes, such as sending an email, are allowed after human confirmation of the recipient and body.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What tasks should I not take on without permission, and which permission options are appropriate for those tasks?

checks.q: Pair the following permission options with actions:
right: Automatically approve low-risk tasks and confirm or reject high-risk tasks.
Ask first for both reads and changes
Executes without approval, so risks are high
Doesn't ask for reading, asks before changing
checks.explain: As options are released, the number of approval steps decreases. This setting does not change account linking or provider permissions themselves and workspace policies may take precedence.
checks.intro: As permission options are unlocked, the number of approval steps decreases. Match options and actions.
checks.correctFeedback: That's correct. The four options were categorized by asking which stage to read or change.
checks.incorrectFeedback: There is a mismatched pair. Approval is reduced in the following order: the option to ask for everything, the option to not ask to read, the option to depend on risk, and the option to run without approval.

checks.q: What is the most appropriate process when entrusting the task of ‘send a schedule change email to my client tomorrow morning’ to an agent?
options: Reading and sending previous emails are considered to have the same read permission and are not asked.
Since sending is a change process, confirm the recipient, time, and text before approving.
Since you have connected your personal account, you can automatically send work emails as well.
Since you have installed the plugin, you can skip account verification.
checks.explain: Reading contacts and previous emails is reading, and sending is execution. It is difficult to return once sent, so do this after approval.

wrong.0: Reading and execution are distinct, and sending corresponds to execution.
wrong.2: Personal accounts only show what the account has access to.
wrong.3: Installing the plugin does not replace account verification or workspace authorization.

checks.intro: Sending mail is a different kind of task than reading. Choose the processing method that suits you.
checks.correctFeedback: That's right. Since sending is a change that is difficult to reverse, check the recipient, time, and body before approving.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Reading and sending old emails are not the same. Please remember that account linking or installation does not replace approval.
